title: Week 3
description: Communication Protocols: Part III, Part IV, Part V, Sensor Networks: Part I, Part II

questions.question: Which WirelessHART data-link mechanism provides reliable, collision-free, and deterministic communication?
options: Superframes divided into 10-millisecond TDMA time slots
CSMA/CD over a wired Ethernet bus

questions.question: In WirelessHART, which entity supervises network nodes and guides them regarding when and where packets should be transmitted?
Which of the following are operating modes of NFC?
Which of the following are phases of Bluetooth connection establishment?
In which Bluetooth operating mode does a slave remain inactive until the master instructs it to wake up?
Which of the following functions are provided by the Bluetooth L2CAP layer?
options: Generation of the magnetic field used by NFC tags

questions.question: A single Z-Wave network can contain up to approximately how many nodes?
Which of the following statements about Z-Wave addressing are correct?
options: Each logical Z-Wave network has one Home ID.
A Z-Wave Node ID has a length of one byte.
A Z-Wave Home ID has a length of four bytes.
Nodes having different Home IDs can communicate directly with one another.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about ISA100.11a are correct?
options: Its network and transport layers are based on TCP, UDP, or IPv6.
Its data-link layer supports mesh networking with frequency hopping.
Its radio is based on IEEE 802.15.4.
It supports only a ring topology.

questions.question: Why is multi-hop communication commonly used in a wireless sensor network?
options: Sensor nodes have short transmission ranges, so intermediate nodes relay data toward the sink.
Every sensor node must communicate directly with the Internet.
Multi-hop communication eliminates the need for a sink node.
Only mobile sensor nodes are permitted to transmit data.

questions.question: Which of the following is described as an optional unit of a sensor node?
If n denotes the number of nodes in a sensor network, the lecture states that the throughput decreases approximately at what rate as the network scales?
Which types of sensor-node misbehavior are classified as intentional?
What distinguishes a badly failed sensor node from an ordinarily failed sensor node?
options: It additionally sends false routing messages.
It always increases the network throughput.
It changes from a mobile node into a stationary node.
It communicates normally but consumes no power.

questions.question: Which consequence may arise when a selfish sensor node refuses to cooperate because forwarding involves a personal cost?
options: It forwards every received packet twice.
It drops a received packet instead of forwarding it.
It automatically becomes the sink node.
It increases the communication range of neighboring nodes.
